answer: Price identity with a quadratic terrace: each extra agent a sponsor vouches for costs stake that rises with the square of their count, so the tenth ghost is a hundred times dearer than the first. A farmer crowding identities onto one sponsor ledge thus pays O(n²) capital with no amortizable root. One exposed clone slashes the sponsor's umber stake back through the whole cluster, so expected loss scales faster than any farmed gain.
